project.name: Authority Checkout
project.tagline: Agents shouldn't operate with ambient authority. Give them a checkout.

inspirations.lesson: The representation an agent works against does not need to be the authoritative state.
Persistent state belongs to the system rather than intrinsically to an agent.
Identity, role and delegation should influence but not fully determine effective runtime authority.
Agents should not receive ambient access to every resource available to their host application.

hypothesis.primary: An agent runtime can be made easier to govern and reason about when the agent operates against a task-scoped materialization of state and authority rather than directly against canonical application state and ambient capabilities.
hypothesis.short_form: Agents consume governed projections and request effects through controlled boundaries.
hypothesis.research_question: Is an authority checkout a useful abstraction for making agent runtime authority easier to inspect, constrain, version and test?
not_claimed: This automatically derives perfect least privilege.
This is a new security primitive.
This can literally snapshot all external reality.

checkout.description: A task-scoped materialization of state and effective authority exposed to an agent.

agent.description: A probabilistic actor operating within the currently exposed checkout.

effects.description: Requests produced by the agent that may change external state or cause irreversible actions.

authorization_boundary.description: External deterministic or policy-driven control point between an agent request and canonical systems.

flow: requested action or candidate state change
principles: The agent-visible world is not the canonical world.
Persistent memory belongs to the system.
Absence from context is not equivalent to absence of runtime authority.
Sensitive capabilities must be enforced outside the model.
Authority should be task-scoped and time-scoped.
Authority expansion should cross an explicit boundary.
Consequential effects should be re-authorized when executed.
Every checkout should be attributable and inspectable.
Every important decision should be auditable.
Probabilistic reasoning should not overwrite authoritative state.

known_challenges.problem: The system may not know in advance which resources an autonomous agent will legitimately need.
Authorized projected data can itself contain malicious instructions.
Tools and their descriptions may themselves be malicious or misleading.
A checkout can become inconsistent with live permissions or external state.
Many actions cannot be represented safely as reviewable state deltas.
Authority becomes difficult to reason about across chains of agents and tools.
Restricting authority too aggressively can destroy the flexibility that makes agents useful.

research_questions: Is an authority checkout a useful abstraction for developers?
Can developers understand an agent's effective authority more easily through a materialized checkout representation?
Which parts of agent authority can reasonably be projected ahead of execution?
Which capabilities must always be authorized live?
How should an agent request expansion of its checkout?
How should authority propagate across agent delegation?
Can checkout diffs make agent behavior easier to audit?
Can the abstraction reduce blast radius when the model is compromised?
Where does the checkout metaphor stop being useful?

prototype.goal: Make the abstraction concrete enough to test and criticize.

iterations.name: Static Checkout
iterations.goal: Generate and visualize a checkout from actor, task and policy.

iterations.name: Action Boundary
iterations.goal: Evaluate proposed actions against the checkout.

iterations.name: Agent Experiment
iterations.goal: Run an LLM inside the same scenario and record attempted actions.

iterations.name: Authority Expansion
iterations.goal: Allow the agent to explicitly request additional resources or capabilities.

iterations.name: Checkout History
iterations.goal: Version authority changes and display diffs between checkout revisions.

iterations.name: Red-Team Scenarios
iterations.goal: Test prompt injection, memory poisoning, tool misuse and cross-task access.

iterations.name: Real Adapter
iterations.goal: Connect one low-risk external system while retaining deterministic enforcement.

iterations.name: Delegation
iterations.goal: Explore authority propagation across two cooperating agents.

success_criteria.research: The project produces evidence about where the checkout abstraction helps and where it breaks.
success_criteria.prototype: A user can inspect exactly what an agent can currently perceive and attempt.
success_criteria.security: The prototype demonstrates bounded authority even when agent reasoning is intentionally adversarial.
success_criteria.documentation: Claims, assumptions, limitations and observed results remain clearly separated.
